section_summary: This section (pages 1–46) comprises State Department despatches, GHQ SCAP bulletins, memoranda, and correspondence from July to September 1949 regarding Japanese tax policy, administration, and enforcement under the Allied Occupation. It focuses heavily on protests by the American Chamber of Commerce in Japan against oppressive corporate taxes, personal income taxes, and import duties on commercial entrants, as well as proposals for bilateral tax conventions. Additionally, it documents SCAP's Internal Revenue Division efforts to modernize the national tax administration, track revenue collections, address tax evasion by United Nations nationals, and prepare for the Shoup Taxation Mission's comprehensive reform report.

subfiles.about: Letter from Leo W. Chamberlain providing detailed paragraph-by-paragraph comments on Henry Shavell's memorandum regarding Japanese taxation of foreign commercial entrants.
subfiles.from: Leo W. Chamberlain, Acting President, The American Chamber of Commerce in Japan
subfiles.summary: Chamberlain provides extensive commentary on Henry Shavell's memorandum regarding Japanese taxation of commercial entrants, arguing that excessive taxes and prewar-style regulations prevent vital foreign capital investment. He opposes taxing dollar incomes at punitive rates, criticizes high tariffs and consumption taxes on personal necessities as damaging to foreign goodwill, and maintains that sales for foreign currency represent valuable exports. He concludes that Japan must grant substantial tax exemptions to foreign businesses and nationals to foster economic recovery.
subfiles.title: Letter from Leo W. Chamberlain to L. H. Moss Regarding Japanese Taxation of Commercial Entrants
subfiles.to: L. H. Moss, Chief, Internal Revenue Division, ESS, GHQ, SCAP

subfiles.about: Letter from Leo W. Chamberlain presenting the views of the American Chamber of Commerce in Japan protesting oppressive Japanese corporation taxes, personal income taxes, and import duties.
subfiles.from: Leo W. Chamberlain, Acting President, American Chamber of Commerce in Japan
keywords: American Chamber of Commerce in Japan
subfiles.summary: Representing a committee of the American Chamber of Commerce in Japan, Chamberlain protests that oppressive corporate, individual income, and real property taxes severely discourage foreign business and investment. The letter criticizes arbitrary tax enforcement, unreasonable automobile levies, and high import tariffs on essential food and clothing unavailable locally. It urges SCAP to prevent Allied nationals from paying for Japanese war rehabilitation by reinstating 1930-1934 tariff schedules or declaring a tax moratorium.

subfiles.to: Major General W. F. Marquat, Chief, Economic & Scientific Section, GHQ, SCAP

subfiles.about: Monthly bulletin disseminating information on Japanese tax administration reforms, newly established tax agencies, revenue collections, and enforcement policies.
subfiles.from: Internal Revenue Division, Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ, SCAP
subfiles.summary: The inaugural monthly bulletin outlines four newly established tax agencies, twenty experimental 'Example' tax offices, and national tax collections exceeding budget estimates for fiscal year 1948-1949. It warns that tax evasion by United Nations nationals will face criminal prosecution in Military Occupation Courts and reports liquor tax rules for Occupation personnel. Furthermore, it details the establishment of the Local Autonomy Agency, local tax amendments, and production and cost-accounting improvements in the Tobacco Monopoly.
subfiles.title: ESS Tax Bulletin, Volume I, No. 1
